indicators.title: Partnerships for the goals: publications
indicators.subtitle: Scholarly Publications Advancing SDG Partnerships
description: The university produces substantial interdisciplinary research addressing global sustainability, governance frameworks, multi-stakeholder partnerships, and cross-sectoral development models.

Publications under SDG 17 analyze collaborative strategies, public-private partnerships, civil society mobilization, and measurable impact mechanisms supporting the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

Kristu Jayanti University, Bengaluru, is one of the institutions the United Nations Academic Impact (UNAI) appointed as an SDG Hub. The university leads Hub 1 (No Poverty) and Hub 10 (Reduced Inequalities), giving it a mandate to advance sustainable development through higher education, research, and community engagement.

This indicator rewards evidence of SDG policy development with government, cross-sectoral dialogue with government or NGOs, international collaboration data gathering for SDG, collaboration for SDG best practice, and collaboration with NGOs for SDGs.

International collaboration: Membership of the global UNAI hub network, working alongside institutions such as York University, Canada, and De Montfort University, UK, demonstrates international data gathering and exchange of best practice.
NGO and community partnership: Hub 1 village outreach, volunteering and student clubs show collaboration with communities and NGOs to address poverty and inequality.
Education and dialogue: SDG Impact Hours, webinars and consultations with UNAI officials show ongoing cross-sector dialogue.
Public evidence: The university publishes an SDG policy and event records online. THE gives extra credit when evidence is public and verifiable.

contentBlocks.title: 2. KRISYM 2025 - Silver Jubilee International Conference The Future of Business Resurgence: Embracing AI and Automation
paragraphs: The International Conference on "The Future of Business Resurgence: Embracing AI and Automation"  was conducted on 16 th & 17th January, 2026. The conference was organised with the objective of exploring the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Automation in reshaping business models and fostering innovation across various industries. It provided an academic platform for scholars, industry experts, academicians, research scholars, and students to discuss the emerging trends, opportunities, and challenges associated with the integration of AI-driven technologies into business operations and management practices. A major focus of the conference was to examine the strategic significance of AI and Automation in transforming traditional business models and encouraging innovative practices across industries. Discussions highlighted how emerging technologies are revolutionising business processes, creating new opportunities for growth, and enabling organisations to adapt to the rapidly evolving digital business environment.

contentBlocks.title: 3. University of Auckland, New Zealand: International Conference on Asia's Maritime History and Identity at Cultural Crossroads.
paragraphs: The Department of English organised the International Conference on Asia's Maritime History and Identity at Cultural Crossroads on 23/01/2025 & 24/01/2025. The conference was organised with the objective of exploring the rich maritime history of Asia, examining its interconnected identities and cultures, and encouraging interdisciplinary discussions on maritime ecosystems and environmental sustainability. It provided an academic platform for scholars, researchers, academicians, and students to engage in meaningful discussions on the historical, cultural, social, and ecological dimensions of maritime studies.  The conference was inaugurated by the distinguished Shaurya Chakra Col. Dr. DPK Pillay, Former Senior Defence Specialist and Planning Officer Defence Ministry and Research Fellow at Manohar Parikkar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses, New Delhi. Fr. Dr Lijo P. Thomas, Vice Principal, Kristu Jayanti College, presided over the event and emphasised that the insights from the conference would help navigate our complex identities of today. In his keynote speech, Col. Dr. DPK Pillay addressed the interconnectedness of different Asian civilisations through trade, exploration, and the movement of people. There were 184 beneficiaries.

contentBlocks.title: 4.  Helik Advisory Limited, Mumbai, India: Guruvani – Insights from the Masters of Forensic Science
paragraphs: The Department of Forensic Science, School of Biological and Forensic Sciences, Kristu Jayanti University, organised a guest lecture titled “Guruvani- Insights from the Masters of Forensic Science” on 13th October 2025 at 12:00 noon in Audi M4, 4th Floor, Science Block. The esteemed resource person for the session was Dr. Rukmani Krishnamurthy, the first eminent lady forensic scientist of the country and Chairperson of Helik Advisory Lab, Pune.

The session witnessed active participation from 81 beneficiaries comprising M.Sc. Forensic Science students from both first and second year. Dr. Krishnamurthy shared valuable insights from her extensive professional journey in forensic science and emphasized the importance of ethical practices and precision in forensic investigations. She elaborated on various career opportunities, emerging research areas, and interdisciplinary approaches within the field. The students enthusiastically interacted with her, raising queries about job prospects, research collaborations, and current trends in forensic science.

Dr. Krishnamurthy also discussed recent developments and news in the forensic domain, inspiring students to stay updated with scientific advancements. The session was highly informative and motivational, enriching students’ understanding of the vast potential and evolving nature of Forensic Science in India.

contentBlocks.title: 6.   Aerospace & Aviation Sector Skill Council, Bengaluru: Importance of AASSC & Skill-Based Job Roles and Credit-Based Certification
paragraphs: The Department of Professional Management Studies, School of Business and Management, Kristu Jayanti University, organized a workshop on “Importance of AASSC & Skill-Based Job Roles and Credit-Based Certification” for the students of BBA Aviation Management. The workshop was conducted in association with the Aerospace and Aviation Sector Skill Council (AASSC)on 21st February 2026 at A2 Auditorium. The students from BBA Aviation Management A and B sections of II and IV semesters actively participated in the programme. The session commenced with an introduction highlighting the growing importance of skill-based education in the aviation industry. The resource persons shared valuable insights into industry-relevant job roles and certification frameworks in the aerospace and aviation sector. The speakers elaborated on the role of AASSC in aligning academic learning with industry requirements. Credit-based certification pathways and their impact on employability were clearly explained. Practical experiences from organizations such as HAL, Air India SATS, and AASSC enriched the discussion. Students actively engaged with the speakers through interactive discussions and queries. The workshop concluded by emphasizing the importance of skill development for career advancement in the aviation industry.

contentBlocks.text: Year 2025

Kristu Jayanti Deemed to be University actively promotes international research collaboration through joint publications and academic engagement with researchers and institutions across national boundaries. These collaborations contribute to the generation, analysis and dissemination of research findings that address global challenges and support the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

The University’s international research collaborations bring together faculty members and researchers from diverse geographical and academic backgrounds to undertake interdisciplinary research. Through joint research publications, knowledge exchange and collaborative academic initiatives, these partnerships facilitate the sharing of research expertise, comparative perspectives and findings relevant to sustainable development.

The collaborative research spans diverse subject areas, with potential contributions to SDG-related themes such as quality education, good health and well-being, industry, innovation and infrastructure, environmental sustainability and social development. Co-authored research publications with international collaborators provide opportunities to examine challenges from different regional and global perspectives, strengthen research outcomes and contribute to the wider academic knowledge base.

Through these international research engagements, Kristu Jayanti Deemed to be University strengthens its global academic connections and supports the exchange of knowledge across institutions and countries. These collaborations contribute to evidence-based research, promote cross-cultural academic understanding and reinforce the University's commitment to research that addresses issues relevant to sustainable development.

contentBlocks.title: 1. University American College, Skopje, North Macedonia - International Conference on Business Transformation through AI
paragraphs: The 3rd International Conference on Business Transformation through AI: A Multidisciplinary Approach commenced with a formal inauguration that set an inspiring tone for the event. The session was graced by Fr. Dr. Augustine George, Vice Chancellor, who delivered the Presidential Address emphasizing the strategic role of artificial intelligence in shaping future-ready institutions. The Inaugural Address was delivered by Mr. Ramesh Balasubramanian, Vice President, Capgemini, who served as the Chief Guest and shared valuable industry-driven insights. He highlighted that technology is not intended to replace human effort but to enhance human experience and organizational efficiency. The welcome address was delivered by Dr. C. Surendranadha Reddy, followed by the ceremonial lighting of the lamp. A soulful prelude performance was presented by Rupashree, adding cultural richness to the occasion. The speakers emphasized the importance of customer-centric innovation, value creation, and automation through AI. Key discussions focused on eliminating inefficiencies, standardizing processes, and leveraging AI for intelligent automation. The session concluded with the message that creativity and critical thinking remain irreplaceable human strengths in an AI-driven era.
Session on creativity and critical thinking in an AI-driven era.

contentBlocks.title: 2. KRISYM 2025 - Silver Jubilee International Conference The Future of Business Resurgence: Embracing AI and Automation
paragraphs: The International Conference on "The Future of Business Resurgence: Embracing AI and Automation"  was conducted on 16 th & 17th January, 2026. The conference was organised with the objective of exploring the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Automation in reshaping business models and fostering innovation across various industries. It provided an academic platform for scholars, industry experts, academicians, research scholars, and students to discuss the emerging trends, opportunities, and challenges associated with the integration of AI-driven technologies into business operations and management practices. A major focus of the conference was to examine the strategic significance of AI and Automation in transforming traditional business models and encouraging innovative practices across industries. Discussions highlighted how emerging technologies are revolutionising business processes, creating new opportunities for growth, and enabling organisations to adapt to the rapidly evolving digital business environment.
Mr. Ramesh Gupta Interacting with Audience

contentBlocks.title: 3. University of Auckland, New Zealand: International Conference on Asia's Maritime History and Identity at Cultural Crossroads.
paragraphs: The Department of English organised the International Conference on Asia's Maritime History and Identity at Cultural Crossroads on 23/01/2025 & 24/01/2025. The conference was organised with the objective of exploring the rich maritime history of Asia, examining its interconnected identities and cultures, and encouraging interdisciplinary discussions on maritime ecosystems and environmental sustainability. It provided an academic platform for scholars, researchers, academicians, and students to engage in meaningful discussions on the historical, cultural, social, and ecological dimensions of maritime studies.  The conference was inaugurated by the distinguished Shaurya Chakra Col. Dr. DPK Pillay, Former Senior Defence Specialist and Planning Officer Defence Ministry and Research Fellow at Manohar Parikkar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses, New Delhi. Fr. Dr Lijo P. Thomas, Vice Principal, Kristu Jayanti College, presided over the event and emphasised that the insights from the conference would help navigate our complex identities of today. In his keynote speech, Col. Dr. DPK Pillay addressed the interconnectedness of different Asian civilisations through trade, exploration, and the movement of people. There were 184 beneficiaries.

contentBlocks.title: 3. University–Community Partnership with Brothers Integrated Rural Development Society (BIRDS) for Digital Awareness and Empowerment of Urban Slum Students
paragraphs: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru, through its Department of Social Work, collaborated with Brothers Integrated Rural Development Society (BIRDS) to organise a Community Organisation Programme titled “Social Media Awareness and Its Impact for Urban Slum Students” on 23 September 2025 at Maria Tuition Centre, Jalahalli. The initiative engaged 30 urban slum students and focused on promoting digital literacy, responsible social media usage, and awareness of online risks and challenges. With the support of BIRDS, the programme provided an interactive learning platform through expert-led awareness sessions and chart presentations, encouraging students to develop critical thinking, responsible digital behaviour, and healthy online habits. This collaboration demonstrates Kristu Jayanti University's commitment to strengthening partnerships with community-based organisations to address digital inequalities, empower underserved communities, and promote inclusive social development. The initiative contributes to SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals, while advancing SDG 4: Quality Education and SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities through collaborative community education and digital empowerment.

contentBlocks.title: 4. NGO Collaboration with Sneha Jyothi Ashraya for Child Rights Awareness and Protection
paragraphs: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru, through its Department of Social Work, collaborated with Sneha Jyothi Ashraya, a non-governmental organisation (NGO) dedicated to the care and support of vulnerable children, to organise a Community Organisation Programme on “Child Rights and Protection” on 29 October 2025 at Sneha Jyothi Ashraya, Bengaluru. The initiative involved 11 Social Work students and focused on creating awareness among children, including orphans and children with special needs, about their fundamental rights, personal safety, self-expression, and mutual respect. Through interactive discussions, storytelling, and participatory activities, the programme empowered children to recognise safe and unsafe situations, express their concerns confidently, and understand the importance of seeking support when required. This collaboration highlights Kristu Jayanti University's commitment to working with NGOs and community-based organisations to promote child welfare, protection, and social inclusion. The initiative contributes to SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals, while supporting SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities and SDG 4: Quality Education through inclusive awareness and community-based learning.

contentBlocks.title: 5. NGO Collaboration with Christel House India and Eco-Watch for Environmental Awareness and Pollution Prevention
paragraphs: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru, through its Department of Social Work, collaborated with Christel House India and Eco-Watch NGO, Jayanagar, Bengaluru, to organise a Community Organisation Programme titled “Preventing Air and Water Pollution for a Healthier Future” on 31 October 2025 at Ashraya Nagar, Peenya. The initiative focused on creating environmental awareness among parents regarding the harmful effects of air and water pollution on human health and the environment. Mr. D. Sujeet Kumar, Programme Manager, Eco-Watch NGO, served as the resource person and sensitised participants on practical environmental conservation measures, including tree planting, reducing plastic consumption, waste management, and water conservation. The programme encouraged active parental participation, responsible environmental practices, and community-level action towards pollution prevention. This collaborative initiative demonstrates Kristu Jayanti University's commitment to strengthening partnerships with NGOs and community organisations to address environmental challenges and promote sustainable living. It contributes to SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals, while directly supporting SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, and SDG 13: Climate Action.

This collaboration reflects Kristu Jayanti University's commitment to strengthening partnerships with NGOs and educational institutions to promote community health, preventive healthcare, and child well-being. contentBlocks.title: VICE CHANCELLOR'S MESSAGE
Vice Chancellor's Message – Glimpses Sustainability Chronicle
paragraphs: It gives me immense joy to pen a few words for Glimpses, which encapsulates the dynamic journey of our institution. This edition holds a special significance, for it mirrors not only the achievements of the past year but also the transformative phase we are stepping into as a deemed to be university.

Becoming a university is a historic milestone in our institutional journey. It signifies growth, maturity, and a renewed responsibility to provide education that transcends boundaries. As a university, we are now better positioned to expand the frontiers of knowledge, promote interdisciplinary learning, strengthen our research culture, and create global platforms for innovation, dialogue, and collaboration. This transition is not just an institutional change but a promise to our students, faculty, and community that we will strive relentlessly to create leaders and thinkers who shape a better tomorrow.

The past academic year has truly reflected our spirit of growth and commitment, with academic engagements, international collaborations, cultural initiatives, and community service programmes seamlessly enriching campus life. From knowledge-driven lectures and faculty development initiatives to vibrant fests and student-led activities, each endeavour has enhanced creativity, diversity, and innovation. At the same time, our social outreach efforts have reinforced our responsibility to society, empowering students to grow as compassionate leaders and responsible citizens who embody the values of justice, inclusivity, and sustainability.

As we embrace the future, the road ahead is filled with immense possibilities. Our focus as a university will be on strengthening research and innovation, nurturing entrepreneurship, advancing digital and technological competencies, and building an ecosystem of sustainability and social responsibility. We envision our university as a space where young minds are not only trained to excel professionally but are also inspired to live meaningfully, with courage, empathy, and wisdom.

I extend my heartfelt appreciation to the editorial team of Glimpses for their tireless efforts in compiling this chronicle of our achievements. May this magazine continue to be a source of inspiration for students, faculty, alumni, and well-wishers, reminding us of the collective spirit that defines our institution and now, our university.

paragraphs: The National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of Kristu Jayanti College organised Shiksha Setu at Government Primary School, K. contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Health and Hygiene Awareness
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Grace, organised a Community Organisation Programme on 'Health and Hygiene' at Grace Pre-school, Old Bagalur Layout, Bengaluru, on 31 October 2025. The programme aimed to create awareness among women and children about the importance of maintaining personal and environmental hygiene and adopting healthy practices in everyday life. Mr. Don Bosco Anthony, Director, Grace, served as the resource person and highlighted the significance of cleanliness, personal hygiene, and preventive health practices. The session focused on basic hygiene practices, their role in preventing common diseases, and the importance of promoting healthy habits within families and communities. The programme also included action songs involving parents and students, followed by an interactive discussion and evaluation.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Healthy Lifestyle and Obesity Prevention
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Liza's Home, organised a Community Organisation Programme titled 'Healthy Habits, Healthy Lives: Combating Obesity' at Liza's Home, Doddagubbi, Bengaluru, on 31 October 2025. The programme aimed to create awareness among individuals with intellectual disabilities and their caregivers about the importance of maintaining a healthy lifestyle, balanced nutrition, and regular healthy habits. Dr. Subramanian, Gynaecologist, served as the resource person and delivered an interactive session on obesity, its associated health concerns, and the significance of adopting healthy lifestyle practices. Using simple explanations and relatable examples, the resource person ensured that the residents could understand the importance of healthy living. The interactive session encouraged active participation from both residents and caregiving staff.

The programme directly contributes to SDG 3 - Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.4, which focuses on promoting health and well-being through the prevention of non-communicable diseases and the encouragement of healthy lifestyles. By addressing obesity prevention, balanced nutrition, and healthy daily routines, the initiative promoted preventive healthcare and improved health awareness among individuals with intellectual disabilities. It also emphasised the role of caregivers in supporting healthy lifestyle choices and ensuring the overall well-being of vulnerable individuals.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Personal Hygiene and Healthy Living
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with FIDES (Family Integral Development Education Scheme), organised a community outreach programme titled 'Swachcha Jeevana, Arogyakara Jeevana (Clean Life, Healthy Life)' at Avalahalli Water Tank Community, Bengaluru, on 2 November 2025. The programme was conducted by first-year MSW students under the guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce, with the objective of promoting personal hygiene, environmental cleanliness, and healthy lifestyle practices among children. The programme featured a colouring competition for children aged 6-10 years on the theme 'Health and Hygiene' and a poster-making competition for children aged 11-15 years on 'Clean Environment and Healthy Living'. Dr. Shobha Rani, Tutor at Ambedkar Medical College, conducted an interactive awareness session on personal hygiene, cleanliness, and healthy habits. A live demonstration of proper brushing techniques and an informative chart presentation helped children understand practical hygiene practices. The programme concluded with prize distribution and refreshments.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 3 - Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.3, through awareness of disease prevention and Target 3.4, through the promotion of healthy lifestyle practices. By educating children on personal hygiene, proper dental care, nutritious food, and preventive health habits, the programme strengthened health awareness from an early age. It also encouraged children to become agents of change by sharing healthy practices with their families and peers, thereby extending the impact of health education into the wider community.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Hygiene Awareness and Healthy Living
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Sumangali Seva Ashrama, organised a community awareness programme titled 'Clean Families, Healthy Children and Brighter Future' on 3 November 2025 at the Community Hall, Kuntigrama Gosai Street, R.T. Nagar, Bengaluru. The programme was organised for members of a rag-picking community comprising approximately 120 families, with the objective of creating awareness about personal hygiene, environmental cleanliness, children's health, and the importance of education. Following preliminary community visits and a needs assessment, the MSW trainees identified poor hygiene practices, inadequate awareness of sanitation, and limited parental involvement in children's education as key concerns. Mrs. Rajeshwari, Health Educator and Social Worker at Cholanayakanahalli UPHC, served as the resource person and conducted an awareness session on maintaining personal and household hygiene, promoting healthy living practices, and ensuring a clean environment for children's development. The programme encouraged active participation, interaction, and collective responsibility among community members.

The initiative primarily contributes to SDG 3 - Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.3, by promoting awareness of preventive health practices and the importance of hygiene in reducing the risk of communicable diseases. It also supports Target 3.9 by addressing health risks associated with unhygienic living conditions and environmental pollution. Through community education and awareness, the programme encouraged families to adopt healthier household practices and recognise the relationship between environmental cleanliness and children's physical well-being. The initiative further strengthened community participation and encouraged parents to take responsibility for creating healthier living conditions for future generations.

contentBlocks.title: 1. Community Outreach Programme on Stress Management for Nursing Students
paragraphs: The community organisation programme on Stress Management for GDA Nursing Students was conducted to create awareness about the causes, symptoms, and effects of stress and to equip students with practical coping strategies for academic and personal challenges. The session, led by Sr Leema, addressed stress management, time management, relaxation techniques, positive thinking, and self-confidence. Interactive discussions and relaxation exercises encouraged active participation and enabled students to identify sources of stress and explore effective coping mechanisms.

The programme directly contributes to SDG 3 - Good Health and Well-being, particularly by promoting mental health awareness and emotional well-being among young learners. It encouraged students to recognise stress, communicate their concerns, and adopt healthy coping practices. The initiative also demonstrated the application of social work knowledge through counselling principles, communication, group facilitation, and community engagement.

contentBlocks.title: Awareness Session on Drug Abuse and Rehabilitation
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, School of Humanities and Social Sciences, Kristu Jayanti College, in collaboration with BREADS (Bangalore Rural Educational and Developmental Society), a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), under the MINDS Project, organised an Awareness Session on Drug Abuse and Rehabilitation on 4 November 2025, from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM, at Mariam Nivas High School, 10, Milton Street, D Costa Layout, Cooke Town, Bengaluru - 560005. The programme was conducted by first-year MSW student trainees (25MSWA17 and 25MSWA36) under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce. Ms. Pranitha P. S., Project Coordinator at BREADS, served as the resource person and addressed the causes and consequences of substance abuse among adolescents, preventive strategies, early intervention and the importance of rehabilitation and community support. Through interactive discussions and real-life examples, the session sensitised students to the harmful effects of drug abuse, peer influence and the importance of healthy coping mechanisms. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, particularly the prevention of substance abuse and the promotion of mental health and well-being. The collaboration with BREADS and its MINDS Project demonstrates the university's partnership with an NGO in strengthening community-based mental health awareness, preventive education and rehabilitation initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Emotional Well-Being Among the Elderly
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), organised an Awareness Session on Emotional Well-Being Among the Elderly on 13 November 2025 at Grace Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, with the participation of first-year MSW student trainees (25MSWA29 and 25MSWA31) under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce. Dr. Sandra K. S., Medical Officer and Manager at Grace Hospital, served as the resource person and conducted an interactive session addressing common emotional and psychological challenges experienced during old age, including loneliness, anxiety and depression. The session highlighted the importance of emotional stability, stress management, self-care, positive thinking and family and community support in promoting healthy ageing. Through interactive discussions and experience-sharing, elderly participants were encouraged to express their feelings, recognise emotional health concerns and adopt appropriate coping strategies. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, particularly the promotion of mental health, psychological well-being and healthy ageing. The programme also strengthened community awareness of the emotional needs of older adults and reinforced the university's commitment to inclusive, community-oriented health and well-being initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Building Emotional Resilience Among Mothers of Children with Special Needs
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Tamahar Trust, Bengaluru, a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), organised a Community Organisation Programme titled "Building Emotional Resilience" on 14 November 2025, from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM, at Tamahar Outreach, Madanayakanahalli, Bengaluru, benefiting 15 mothers of children with special needs. The programme was organised by II MSW students, with Ms. Gayatri Rao, Consultant Psychologist at Tamahar Trust, serving as the resource person. The session focused on strengthening the emotional resilience of caregivers by addressing stress management, self-care, positive communication, healthy coping mechanisms and the importance of family and community support networks. Interactive discussions and experience-sharing activities provided mothers with a supportive platform to express their caregiving challenges, develop mutual understanding and overcome feelings of isolation. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, particularly mental health promotion and psychological well-being among caregivers of children with special needs. The collaboration with Tamahar Trust highlights the university's engagement with an NGO in providing community-based emotional support, strengthening caregiver resilience and promoting inclusive health and well-being.

contentBlocks.title: QUALITY EDUCATION
1. Social Media Awareness and Its Impact on Urban Slum Students
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru, in collaboration with Brothers Integrated Rural Development Society (BIRDS), a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), organised a Community Organisation Programme titled "Social Media Awareness and Its Impact for Urban Slum Students" on 23 September 2025 at Maria Tuition Centre, Jalahalli, Bengaluru, benefiting 30 students from the urban slum community. The programme was conducted under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce A, with Mr. Gnana Prakash, Rural Coordinator, serving as the resource person. The session focused on educating students about the positive educational uses of social media, including communication, learning and skill development, while addressing associated risks such as misinformation, excessive usage and irresponsible online behaviour. An interactive chart presentation encouraged students to share their experiences, develop critical thinking and understand the importance of responsible digital practices. The initiative contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting inclusive learning opportunities, digital awareness and the development of essential digital literacy and critical thinking skills among students from an underserved urban community. The collaboration with BIRDS highlights the university's engagement with an NGO in extending educational awareness and digital learning competencies to socially and economically disadvantaged communities.

contentBlocks.title: Innovative Approaches to Mathematics Education
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Akshara Foundation, a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO) working towards improving the quality of education, and Jeeyar Memorial School, organised an educational outreach programme titled "Innovative Approaches to Mathematics Education" on 3 November 2025 at Jeeyar Memorial School, B. Channasandra, Bengaluru. The programme was facilitated by first-year MSW student trainees Christine Anna Kurien and New Life B, under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce. Mr. Shivakumar served as the resource person and introduced innovative, child-friendly and activity-based approaches to mathematics education through games, puzzles, visual aids and hands-on activities focusing on arithmetic operations, logical reasoning and problem-solving skills. The interactive activities encouraged students to participate enthusiastically, develop mathematical curiosity and gain confidence in understanding mathematical concepts. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting inclusive, equitable and effective learning opportunities through experiential and participatory teaching methods. The collaboration with Akshara Foundation highlights the university's partnership with an NGO in strengthening educational outreach and improving learning experiences among school students through innovative pedagogical practices.

contentBlocks.title: Awareness session on "Building Reading Habits In Children "
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Vathsalya Charitable Trust, a non-governmental organisation (NGO), organised a Community Organisation Programme titled "Building Reading Habits in Children" on 4 November 2025 at Vathsalya Charitable Trust, Bengaluru. The programme was facilitated by first-year MSW student trainees Kesang Chhoden and Sreelakshmi Ramesh under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce A. Ms. Santi, Manager of the Community Development Centre (CDC), served as the resource person and highlighted the importance of reading in developing children's knowledge, imagination, creativity, language skills and moral values. Through interactive discussions, storytelling and experience-sharing activities, children were encouraged to explore books, share their favourite stories and develop reading as a regular habit. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting foundational literacy, inclusive learning opportunities and a culture of lifelong learning among children. The collaboration with Vathsalya Charitable Trust highlights the university's engagement with an NGO in strengthening community-based educational initiatives and encouraging reading practices among children. The programme resulted in increased enthusiasm for reading, greater awareness of its educational benefits and motivation among children, teachers and caregivers to sustain regular reading activities.

contentBlocks.title: Life Skills Session - "My Dream, My Future"
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Global Concerns India, a non-governmental organisation (NGO), organised a Life Skills Development Programme titled "My Dream, My Future" on 10 November 2025 at the Global Concerns India - Children Creativity Centre. The programme was facilitated by first-year MSW student trainees (25MSWA01 and 25MSWA25) under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce, with support from Dr. Sadhana Dash Philip, Organisation Supervisor, and Programme Coordinators Ms. Maria Subrahmaniam and Ms. Zeena Mani. The session focused on developing essential life skills, including communication, decision-making, problem-solving, empathy, self-awareness and emotional management, in accordance with the core life skills framework of the World Health Organization (WHO). Through visual presentations, interactive discussions and activities encouraging students to introduce themselves and share their future ambitions, the programme promoted confidence, positive thinking, self-expression and goal-setting. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting inclusive, holistic and learner-centred education through the development of essential life skills and competencies. The collaboration with Global Concerns India highlights the university's partnership with an NGO in extending meaningful educational and personal development opportunities to children through community-based learning initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Awareness session on “Mindful Screen Use - Using Technology Wisely for Learning Purposes."
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, organised a Community Organisation Programme titled "Mindful Screen Use Using Technology Wisely for Learning Purposes" on 11 November 2025 at Sukrupa School Educational Centre, Bengaluru, with the participation of first-year MSW student trainees Annriya J. Kunnath V. S. and Shelly Pyngrope Phawa, under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce A. The session was facilitated by Ms. Mohana Priya, who sensitised students and parents to the productive use of digital technology for learning while addressing the consequences of excessive screen exposure, including reduced concentration, sleep disturbances and increased stress. Through interactive discussions, demonstrations and reflective activities, participants learned practical strategies such as setting screen-time limits, taking regular breaks, selecting educational content and maintaining responsible digital habits. The initiative contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting digital literacy, responsible technology use and equitable access to technology-supported learning. The programme also strengthened awareness among parents and students about creating healthy digital learning environments at home, encouraging technology to serve as an effective educational resource rather than a distraction.

contentBlocks.title: Yuva Avishkar - Workshop on Basics of Electronics and Robotics
paragraphs: The Karnataka Civil Defence Corps of Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous), under Jayantian Extension Services, organised Yuva Avishkar, a 30-hour workshop on the Basics of Electronics and Robotics at Government Higher Primary School, Kothanur, from 20 to 31 January 2025. The programme engaged 50 school students in experiential STEM learning through demonstrations and hands-on activities using electronic components, circuits and robotics kits. Students explored scientific concepts such as LEDs, switches, conductors, electromagnetism, circuit design, atomic structure and astronomy, while developing skills in observation, experimentation, analysis and creative problem-solving. The programme used 15 interactive models and robotics kits, covering more than 20 scientific concepts. Post-activity assessment indicated improved conceptual understanding among 95% of participants, while 90% reported increased interest in STEM and space science. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly Target 4.4, by strengthening the technical and scientific skills of school students through practical, accessible and experiential learning.

contentBlocks.title: Yuva Pathshala: Promoting Inclusive Learning and Educational Support for Children in Underserved Communities
paragraphs: The Karnataka Civil Defence Corps (KCDC) Club of Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), through its Jayantian Extension Services, organised Yuva Pathshala on 16 and 23 October 2025 and 30 October 2025 and 8 January 2026 at Kacharakanahalli and K. Narayanapura slum communities, Bengaluru. The initiative engaged 55 student volunteers in providing educational guidance and interactive learning support to children from economically disadvantaged communities. Through educational game drawing exercises and interactive teaching sessions, the programme aimed to stimulate creativity, strengthen learning interests, enhance confidence and encourage teamwork among the children. The initiative provided supplementary educational engagement in an underserved community, contributing to more inclusive learning opportunities and addressing educational disadvantages. It also enabled student volunteers to develop empathy, communication, teamwork and leadership skills through community engagement. The programme supports SDG 4 (Quality Education), particularly Target 4.5, by promoting educational inclusion and learning support for children in vulnerable circumstances.

contentBlocks.title: Sustainova 2025: Promoting Sustainability Awareness and Education through Student-Led Innovation
paragraphs: The UNAI SDG Hub 10 - Vice-Chair for Teaching and Education of Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) organised Sustainova 2025, an intra-university sustainability fest on 24 September 2025, with the participation of 130 beneficiaries. The initiative provided a student-centred platform to promote awareness and understanding of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals through creative, experiential and collaborative learning. The major events included InnoViron Expo, SDG Policy Architects, Eco Vogue Runway and Quest for 17, encouraging students to explore sustainability challenges and develop innovative responses. As part of the InnoViron Expo, students exhibited creative models representing all 17 SDGs, translating their understanding of global sustainability concerns into practical and visual learning experiences. The programme encouraged critical thinking, innovation, teamwork and responsible citizenship while strengthening students' understanding of sustainable development. Through these educational activities, the university contributed to SDG 4 (Quality Education), particularly Target 4.7, by fostering knowledge, awareness and competencies essential for sustainable development.

contentBlocks.title: GENDER EQUALITY
Insurance for Independence- A financial Safety for Women
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Shishumandir, Bengaluru, organised a community outreach programme titled "Insurance for Independence - Financial Security for Women" on 5 November 2025 at Shishumandir, Bengaluru. The programme was coordinated by first-year MSW students bearing roll numbers 25MSWA12, 25MSWA15 and 25MSWA43, under the guidance of faculty in-charge Dr. Winnie Joyce. Mr. Loganathan S. served as the resource person. The session was conducted for women e-auto drivers to create awareness about the importance of financial protection and independent financial planning. It covered various aspects of life, health and vehicle insurance, including policy benefits, enrolment procedures, premium payments, claim processes and available government and private insurance schemes. The programme aimed to strengthen women's financial literacy, promote informed financial decision-making and improve their access to financial protection mechanisms. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 5: Gender Equality, particularly by supporting women's economic empowerment, financial independence and equal opportunities to access financial services and security mechanisms.

contentBlocks.title: CLEAN WATER AND SANITATION
Community Organisation Programme on "Basic Hygiene and Sanitation for School Children"
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Bosco Nivas, organised a community awareness programme on "Basic Hygiene and Sanitation for School Children" at St. Xavier's High School, Shivajinagar, Bengaluru, on 31 October 2025. The programme educated school children on personal hygiene, proper handwashing techniques, oral hygiene, cleanliness, the use of sanitary toilet facilities, and the importance of safe drinking water. Through interactive discussions, visual demonstrations, and awareness activities, the programme promoted healthy hygiene practices and highlighted their role in preventing communicable diseases. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, particularly Target 6.2, by promoting adequate sanitation and hygiene practices and fostering awareness of their importance in maintaining healthy communities.

contentBlocks.title: Community Organisation Programme on "Fostering Sustainable and Resilient WASH Practices"
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru, in collaboration with SOS Children's Villages India, organised a community awareness programme on "Fostering Sustainable and Resilient WASH Practices" at Lingarajapuram, Bengaluru, on 1 November 2025, benefiting 30 participants. The session, facilitated by Mr. Sathish K. N., Program Manager, Catalyst Management Service, focused on promoting sustainable Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) practices. Through interactive demonstrations, handwashing action songs, animated videos and group drawing activities, children were educated on the importance of safe drinking water, proper sanitation, personal hygiene, responsible water use and maintaining clean surroundings. The programme also highlighted the importance of healthy eating habits in promoting overall well-being. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, particularly Targets 6.1 and 6.2, by strengthening awareness of safe water, sanitation and hygiene practices and encouraging children to adopt responsible behaviours for healthier and more sustainable communities.

contentBlocks.title: DECENT WORK AND ECONOMIC GROWTH
Community Organisation Programme on "Financial Literacy and Career Guidance"
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with MYRADA (Mysore Resettlement and Development Agency), organised a community outreach programme on "Financial Literacy and Career Guidance" at St. Mary's School and Composite PU College, Byrathi, Bengaluru, on 13 November 2025, benefiting 120 students from the Arts, Commerce, Science and Languages streams. Facilitated by Ms. Riya Shaji Mathew, Vocational Trainer and Executive Programme Coordinator at Akshadhaa Foundation, the programme focused on developing students' financial management skills and enhancing awareness of diverse career opportunities. The session covered essential financial concepts, including budgeting, saving and financial planning, while guiding students to make informed career choices based on their interests, aptitude and emerging employment opportunities. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, particularly Target 8.6, by equipping young people with career awareness, employability-related knowledge and essential financial skills, thereby encouraging informed career decisions and supporting their transition towards productive employment and economic independence.

contentBlocks.title: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan - One District One Product (ODOP) Scheme: Campus Farmers' Market (CFM) - Farmers to Students (F2S)
paragraphs: Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous), under Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA), organised the Campus Farmers' Market (CFM) under the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative on 31 January 2025, as part of the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The programme, themed "From Farmers to Students: Growing Knowledge, Nourishing Futures," aimed to strengthen the connection between rural farmers and urban consumers while promoting local agricultural products, rural entrepreneurship and sustainable economic development. The event was inaugurated in the presence of Shri Pradeep Simha, District Officer, Minority Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, and provided a platform for 12 farmers from different districts to showcase and directly market their agricultural produce, organic goods and traditional food products. The Campus Farmers' Market benefited over 5,000 individuals by facilitating access to local produce, promoting farmer-consumer interactions and creating awareness about supporting local agricultural economies. By providing market access to rural producers, encouraging entrepreneurship and reducing intermediary barriers, the initiative directly contributes to SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, particularly Target 8.3, which promotes productive activities, entrepreneurship, innovation and the growth of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. It also supports inclusive economic opportunities and sustainable rural livelihoods.

contentBlocks.title: REDUCED INEQUALITIES
NSS Community Outreach Programme - Visit to Neha Jyothi Ashram
paragraphs: The National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of Kristu Jayanti College organised a community outreach programme at Neha Jyothi Ashram on 8 March 2025, benefiting 15 children. The initiative aimed to promote compassion, social responsibility and inclusive community engagement through donation and interactive activities. NSS volunteers from two student teams collectively mobilised donations worth 2,000 and provided essential items and snacks to the children. The volunteers also engaged the children through storytelling, musical chairs, passing-the-ball games, singing and dancing activities, encouraging their creativity, self-expression and social interaction. Prizes were distributed to the winners, making the visit a joyful and meaningful experience. The initiative fostered a spirit of volunteerism, kindness and community participation while promoting the inclusion and well-being of vulnerable children. The programme contributes to SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, by encouraging the social inclusion and participation of vulnerable groups through community engagement and supportive interventions.

contentBlocks.title: Observation Visit to Manna Trust
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), organised an observation visit to Manna Trust on 1 August 2025 for I MSW students to provide firsthand exposure to the functioning of a voluntary organisation and its interventions for marginalised communities. The visit familiarised students with the organisation's initiatives in education, healthcare, women's empowerment, vocational training and livelihood promotion for underprivileged sections of society. Through interactions with social work professionals and observations of ongoing development programmes, students gained insights into participatory approaches, community empowerment, advocacy and inclusive development practices. The visit also highlighted the role of voluntary organisations in addressing social inequalities and improving access to essential opportunities and services for disadvantaged communities. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, by highlighting community-based interventions that promote the social and economic inclusion of all, irrespective of their background or socioeconomic status.

contentBlocks.title: Harmony in Diversity: Art and Music Activities For Differently Abled Children
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Oceanik Institute of Higher Education, Bengaluru, organised a community engagement programme titled 'Harmony in Diversity: Art and Music Activities for Differently Abled Children' on 1 November 2025. Organised by student trainees Sheetal Pattanashetti and Mohammed Fasil, under the guidance of Mrs. Maheshwari, the programme aimed to promote inclusion, creativity, self-expression, and social interaction among differently abled students, including those with hearing and visual impairments. Facilitated by Dr. N. M. Poovaiah, the session incorporated singing and art activities that provided participants with opportunities to showcase their talents, express themselves creatively, and engage in collaborative experiences. The programme created a supportive and inclusive environment that encouraged confidence, mutual understanding, and meaningful participation among students.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 10 Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, which focuses on empowering and promoting the social inclusion of all individuals, irrespective of age, disability, or other status. By providing differently abled children with equal opportunities to participate in artistic and musical activities, the programme promoted accessibility, recognition of individual abilities, and social integration. It also challenged barriers to participation by creating an inclusive platform where students could express their talents and interact without discrimination. The initiative reflects the University's commitment to disability inclusion, equal opportunities, diversity, and the promotion of an inclusive and equitable society.

contentBlocks.title: Emergency and Safety Skill for Young Adults with Intellectual Disabilities
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, conducted a community awareness programme titled 'Emergency and Safety Skills for Young Adults with Intellectual Disabilities' on 4 November 2025 at Diya Foundation, Bengaluru, involving first-year MSW students. The programme engaged 28 beneficiaries and aimed to enhance their awareness and preparedness in responding to emergencies. The session covered physical, emotional, and personal safety, identification of emergency services, and appropriate responses to situations such as fire accidents, gas leaks, and medical emergencies. Through visual aids, practical explanations, and demonstrations, participants were introduced to emergency contact procedures using the 4 W's, fire safety measures, emergency evacuation practices, basic life-saving techniques, and the importance of seeking immediate assistance. The initiative focused on strengthening the beneficiaries' confidence, independence, and ability to respond safely to emergency situations.

The programme directly contributes to SDG 10 - Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, which aims to empower and promote the social, economic, and political inclusion of all individuals, irrespective of age, disability, or other status. By providing young adults with intellectual disabilities access to essential safety education and practical emergency preparedness skills, the initiative promoted equal access to knowledge, personal security, and independent living. It also addressed the specific learning and safety needs of persons with intellectual disabilities, encouraging their active participation and integration into society. The programme reflects the University's commitment to disability inclusion, empowerment, equal opportunities, and the development of a safer and more supportive community.

contentBlocks.title: Functional and Mobility Movement Session
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, conducted a community organisation programme titled 'Functional and Mobility Movement Session' on 12 November 2025 at Akshadhaa Foundation, involving first-year MSW students. The programme was designed for children with neurological disabilities, with the objective of promoting physical development, mobility, coordination, balance, and overall well-being through structured, play-based activities. Facilitated by Mr. Jyothish, a Bachelor of Physiotherapy intern, the session included warm-up exercises, breathing practices, ball-toss activities, balance exercises, and functional movement tasks. The MSW trainees provided individual guidance and support to ensure the active participation and safety of all children. The activities encouraged the development of motor skills, physical confidence, and functional abilities in an inclusive and supportive environment.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 10 - Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, which aims to empower and promote the social, economic, and political inclusion of all individuals, irrespective of age, disability, or other status. By providing children with neurological disabilities opportunities to participate in structured physical activities, the programme promoted inclusion, equal participation, and access to developmental support. The initiative also helped recognise the abilities and potential of children with disabilities while encouraging an environment that respects individual needs and differences. Through this intervention, the University demonstrated its commitment to disability inclusion, equal opportunities, and the empowerment of vulnerable groups.

contentBlocks.title: Emergency and Safety Skill for Young Adults with Intellectual Disabilities

contentBlocks.title: SUSTAINABLE CITIES AND COMMUNITIES
Launch of 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (VADP) under Unnat Bharat Abhiyan - Viksit Bharat @2047
paragraphs: The Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA), Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous), launched the 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (VADP) on 23 January 2025 as part of the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The initiative aims to promote holistic and sustainable development across 25 adopted villages through community participation, capacity building and integrated rural development. The programme focuses on improving community well-being through health and sanitation initiatives, skill development, women's empowerment, rural entrepreneurship, livelihood promotion and environmental sustainability. It also emphasises strengthening local leadership, encouraging renewable energy adoption, promoting sustainable agricultural practices and improving waste management. By fostering active community participation and addressing the social, economic and environmental needs of rural populations, the initiative seeks to create inclusive, resilient and sustainable communities. The programme contributes to SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities, particularly Target 11.a, by promoting integrated rural development and strengthening the linkages between urban and rural communities through sustainable development initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Fire Safety Awareness Programme and Mock Drill - Karnataka Civil Defence Corps
paragraphs: The Karnataka Civil Defence Corps (KCDC) of Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous), under Jayantian Extension Services, organised a Fire Safety Awareness Programme and Mock Drill on 2 March 2025, benefiting 48 participants, including KCDC volunteers and villagers. The programme was conducted by the Kolar Fire Safety Team, which provided practical demonstrations on fire prevention, the classification and usage of fire extinguishers, and emergency response procedures. Participants gained hands-on exposure to firefighting equipment, fire engines and different types of water hoses through a live mock drill. The session enhanced awareness of fire hazards, emergency preparedness and the importance of timely and coordinated action during fire-related incidents. The initiative strengthened community resilience by equipping volunteers and villagers with essential knowledge and practical skills to respond to emergencies. The programme directly contributes to SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities, particularly Target 11.5, by promoting disaster preparedness and strengthening community-level capacity to reduce the impact of disasters and emergencies.

contentBlocks.title: RESPONSIBLE CONSUMPTION AND PRODUCTION
Zero Waste Management
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Ashalaya Trust, Vidyanagar, Bengaluru, organised a community awareness programme on 'Zero Waste Management' on 4 November 2025 at Ashalaya Auditorium. The programme, facilitated by Mr. Abin Philip, Programme Coordinator, Ashalaya Trust, engaged 48 students in understanding sustainable waste management practices and environmental responsibility. The session focused on waste segregation, recycling, composting, and the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (3Rs). Through interactive discussions, practical demonstrations, group activities, and a pledge-taking session, participants gained practical knowledge of reducing waste generation, minimising plastic consumption, and adopting responsible disposal practices. The initiative encouraged students to integrate sustainable consumption habits into their everyday lives and promote environmental awareness within their communities.

The programme directly contributes to SDG 12 Responsible Consumption and Production, particularly Target 12.5, which aims to substantially reduce waste generation through prevention, reduction, recycling, and reuse. By educating students on waste segregation, material recovery, recycling, and responsible consumption, the initiative promoted practical approaches to minimising waste at the individual and community levels. The programme also supports Target 12.8 by enhancing awareness and knowledge of sustainable lifestyles and environmentally responsible practices. The collaboration with Ashalaya Trust further strengthened community-based environmental education and encouraged behavioural changes towards resource conservation and sustainable living.

contentBlocks.title: PEACE, JUSTICE AND STRONG INSTITUTIONS
Child Rights and Protection
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, conducted a community organisation programme on 'Child Rights and Protection' on 29 October 2025 at Sneha Jyothi Ashraya, Bengaluru, involving 11 students. The programme aimed to sensitise children, including orphans and children with special needs, about their fundamental rights, personal safety, safe and unsafe situations, and the importance of mutual respect. Through interactive discussions, storytelling, simple examples, and question-and-answer activities, the MSW students facilitated an engaging learning environment that encouraged children to express themselves and understand their rights. The session also focused on building children's confidence to communicate concerns and approach trusted individuals for assistance. The programme extended its awareness-building efforts to caregivers and the surrounding community, emphasising their collective responsibility in ensuring children's safety, dignity, and protection.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, particularly Target 16.2, which aims to end abuse, exploitation, trafficking, and all forms of violence against children. By educating children about their rights, personal safety, and mechanisms for seeking help, the programme strengthened awareness of child protection and prevention of abuse. The observed improvement in children's confidence, ability to recognise unsafe situations, and willingness to express themselves highlights the programme's contribution towards fostering a safe, inclusive, and protective environment. The initiative reflects the University's commitment to promoting children's rights, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and strengthening community responsibility towards child protection.

contentBlocks.title: Community Organisation Programme on "Safe Touch and Unsafe Touch"
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with MANNA Centre for Special Needs Children, Bengaluru, organised a community awareness programme on "Safe Touch and Unsafe Touch" on 4 November 2025 for especially abled children. Facilitated by Ms. Nirmala Jacob, Coordinator of Exodus Transitional School, the programme aimed to create awareness about body safety, personal boundaries and child protection through age-appropriate and interactive learning methods. Using skits, discussions and colouring activities, children were sensitised to identifying safe and unsafe physical contact, expressing discomfort, recognising potentially harmful situations and approaching trusted adults for support. The initiative strengthened awareness of child rights, personal safety and preventive measures against abuse and exploitation. The programme directly contributes to SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, particularly Target 16.2, which focuses on ending abuse, exploitation, trafficking and all forms of violence against children.

Courses such as Climate Change and Sustainable Development Goals, Economics of Sustainable Development Goals, Environmental Studies and Conservation, Gender Studies, Introduction to Human Rights and Sustainable Human Resource Management provide opportunities to connect disciplinary knowledge with relevant SDGs and contemporary sustainability challenges.

The multidisciplinary curriculum encourages students to explore sustainability through environmental, economic, social and ethical perspectives. These courses provide a foundation for critical thinking and understanding the interconnected nature of sustainable development. SDG-related courses across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes demonstrate opportunities for sustainability learning in diverse academic disciplines. Curriculum mapping and programme-level documentation can further establish the extent of SDG education available to students across the university.

contentBlocks.text: Integration of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Across Undergraduate and Postgraduate Programmes

Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) is committed to advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by embedding sustainability-oriented knowledge, values and practices across its Undergraduate (UG) and Postgraduate (PG) programmes through relevant courses and curricular components. The programmes listed below incorporate SDG-related themes into their academic curriculum, enabling students to understand and engage with contemporary global sustainability challenges.

Courses offered across Humanities, Social Sciences, Management, Commerce, Science, Biotechnology, Psychology and Economics address the multiple dimensions of sustainable development, including poverty alleviation, food security, health and well-being, quality education, gender equality, decent work, innovation, reduced inequalities, sustainable communities, responsible consumption, climate action, environmental conservation, human rights, ethical governance and global partnerships. By drawing students from diverse academic backgrounds into these themes, the University encourages them to recognise their role in addressing local, national and global development priorities.

The University follows an interdisciplinary, curriculum-integrated approach, in which SDG principles are incorporated into existing disciplinary courses rather than confined to standalone degree programmes. This ensures that students encounter sustainability perspectives within their own fields of study, enabling them to develop subject-specific knowledge, critical awareness, ethical responsibility and the competencies required to contribute meaningfully to sustainable development.
SDG 2 – Zero Hunger

Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) is committed to advancing SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) by integrating food security, sustainable agriculture and rural development into its academic curriculum, in line with Indicator 17.4.2. Through a range of courses spanning agricultural development, plant biotechnology and applied laboratory practice, the institution provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the social, scientific and technological dimensions of food production and hunger reduction. These courses build theoretical knowledge, practical skills and awareness of sustainable agricultural practices, preparing graduates for careers in research, industry and rural development. By embedding these themes in its teaching, the institution equips academics and future generations to contribute to a food-secure and sustainable world.

contentBlocks.text: SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being

Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) is committed to advancing SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) by integrating physical, psychological and social dimensions of health into its academic curriculum, in line with Indicator 17.4.2. Through a diverse set of courses and practicals spanning yoga and wellness, health economics, social psychology, health psychology, positive psychology and rehabilitation psychology, the institution provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the factors that shape individual and community well-being. These courses examine the economic aspects of healthcare and resource allocation, the psychological influences on health, illness and health behaviour, and the role of resilience, strengths and rehabilitation in improving quality of life, while the associated practical components build applied skills in psychological assessment, behavioural understanding and wellness practices. By embedding these themes in its teaching, the institution prepares graduates for careers in healthcare, counselling, rehabilitation and allied fields, and equips academics and future generations to promote healthier and more resilient societies.

These courses develop critical thinking, creative expression and ethical awareness, while also introducing Indian psychological traditions and perspectives on human behaviour and learning, thereby enriching students’ understanding of education within a broader cultural and intellectual context. By integrating these themes into its teaching, the institution prepares graduates to be reflective, skilled and socially responsible individuals, and equips academics and future generations to contribute to a more educated, inclusive and sustainable society.
