contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) takes learning beyond the campus and into the neighbourhoods around it. Through awareness sessions, workshops and community programmes, our students and faculty work with local residents, families in urban slum areas, elderly citizens, women and village communities in and around Bengaluru. The sessions cover topics people use in daily life, such as health and hygiene, clean water and sanitation, fire safety, financial awareness and basic education support. Each programme is planned around the needs of the group it serves and is held in their own locality, so that participation is easy. The activities listed below show how the University links its SDG commitments to practical learning for the wider community
Local Community

contentBlocks.title: NSS Initiative – Shiksha Setu: Supporting School Children through Nutritional and Educational Assistance
paragraphs: The National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of Kristu Jayanti College organised Shiksha Setu at Government Primary School, K. Narayanapura, Bengaluru, on 12 February 2025, benefiting 35 school children. The initiative, conducted under the supervision of Dr. Vinoth B., Assistant Professor, Department of Statistics, aimed to support the well-being and educational engagement of children from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. NSS volunteers facilitated the distribution of snacks and stationery worth ₹3,000, supported through volunteer contributions, to encourage student participation and promote better attentiveness during school hours. The programme also included interactive academic reinforcement and extracurricular learning activities that fostered curiosity and created a supportive learning environment. The initiative contributed to SDG 2: Zero Hunger, particularly Target 2.1, by supporting access to food among school children, and SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly Target 4.1, by encouraging school engagement and supporting children's learning experiences.

contentBlocks.title: SDG-Aligned Community Outreach Initiative: Promoting Environmental Health through Air and Water Pollution Prevention
paragraphs: The Community Organisation Programme on ‘Preventing Air and Water Pollution for a Healthier Future’ was organised at Ashraya Nagar, Peenya, on 31 October 2025, from 11:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon, targeting parents from the local community. Conducted by the Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Christel House India and Eco-Watch NGO, the programme aimed to create awareness about the adverse effects of air and water pollution on human health and the environment. Mr. D. Sujeet Kumar, Programme Manager, Eco-Watch NGO, served as the resource person. The session highlighted the importance of environmental protection through practical measures such as waste segregation, reducing plastic usage, tree planting, and water conservation. Parents actively participated in discussions and expressed their commitment to adopting eco-friendly practices in their households.

The programme primarily contributes to SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) by addressing health risks associated with environmental pollution and SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) by promoting water conservation and pollution prevention. It also supports SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) through community-level environmental responsibility and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by encouraging responsible waste management and reduced plastic consumption. The initiative strengthened environmental awareness, encouraged collective community action, and highlighted the importance of sustainable practices in ensuring a healthier environment for future generations.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Health and Hygiene Awareness
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Grace, organised a Community Organisation Programme on ‘Health and Hygiene’ at Grace Pre-school, Old Bagalur Layout, Bengaluru, on 31 October 2025. The programme aimed to create awareness among women and children about the importance of maintaining personal and environmental hygiene and adopting healthy practices in everyday life. Mr. Don Bosco Anthony, Director, Grace, served as the resource person and highlighted the significance of cleanliness, personal hygiene, and preventive health practices. The session focused on basic hygiene practices, their role in preventing common diseases, and the importance of promoting healthy habits within families and communities. The programme also included action songs involving parents and students, followed by an interactive discussion and evaluation.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.3, through awareness of disease prevention and Target 3.4, through the promotion of healthy lifestyles and overall well-being. By educating parents and children on personal hygiene, cleanliness, and preventive health practices, the programme encouraged positive behavioural changes and strengthened community participation in promoting health and well-being. It also highlighted the important role of parents in developing healthy habits among children and fostering a healthier community.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Healthy Lifestyle and Obesity Prevention
paragraphs: The programme directly contributes to SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.4, which focuses on promoting health and well-being through the prevention of non-communicable diseases and the encouragement of healthy lifestyles. By addressing obesity prevention, balanced nutrition, and healthy daily routines, the initiative promoted preventive healthcare and improved health awareness among individuals with intellectual disabilities. It also emphasised the role of caregivers in supporting healthy lifestyle choices and ensuring the overall well-being of vulnerable individuals.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Personal Hygiene and Healthy Living
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with FIDES (Family Integral Development Education Scheme), organised a community outreach programme titled ‘Swachcha Jeevana, Arogyakara Jeevana (Clean Life, Healthy Life)’ at Avalahalli Water Tank Community, Bengaluru, on 2 November 2025. The programme was conducted by first-year MSW students under the guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce, with the objective of promoting personal hygiene, environmental cleanliness, and healthy lifestyle practices among children. The programme featured a colouring competition for children aged 6–10 years on the theme ‘Health and Hygiene’ and a poster-making competition for children aged 11–15 years on ‘Clean Environment and Healthy Living’. Dr. Shobha Rani, Tutor at Ambedkar Medical College, conducted an interactive awareness session on personal hygiene, cleanliness, and healthy habits. A live demonstration of proper brushing techniques and an informative chart presentation helped children understand practical hygiene practices. The programme concluded with prize distribution and refreshments.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.3, through awareness of disease prevention and Target 3.4, through the promotion of healthy lifestyle practices. By educating children on personal hygiene, proper dental care, nutritious food, and preventive health habits, the programme strengthened health awareness from an early age. It also encouraged children to become agents of change by sharing healthy practices with their families and peers, thereby extending the impact of health education into the wider community.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Hygiene Awareness and Healthy Living
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Sumangali Seva Ashrama, organised a community awareness programme titled ‘Clean Families, Healthy Children and Brighter Future’ on 3 November 2025 at the Community Hall, Kuntigrama Gosai Street, R.T. Nagar, Bengaluru. The programme was organised for members of a rag-picking community comprising approximately 120 families, with the objective of creating awareness about personal hygiene, environmental cleanliness, children's health, and the importance of education. Following preliminary community visits and a needs assessment, the MSW trainees identified poor hygiene practices, inadequate awareness of sanitation, and limited parental involvement in children's education as key concerns. Mrs. Rajeshwari, Health Educator and Social Worker at Cholanayakanahalli UPHC, served as the resource person and conducted an awareness session on maintaining personal and household hygiene, promoting healthy living practices, and ensuring a clean environment for children's development. The programme encouraged active participation, interaction, and collective responsibility among community membersThe initiative primarily contributes to SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.3, by promoting awareness of preventive health practices and the importance of hygiene in reducing the risk of communicable diseases. It also supports Target 3.9 by addressing health risks associated with unhygienic living conditions and environmental pollution. Through community education and awareness, the programme encouraged families to adopt healthier household practices and recognise the relationship between environmental cleanliness and children's physical well-being. The initiative further strengthened community participation and encouraged parents to take responsibility for creating healthier living conditions for future generations.

contentBlocks.title: Health Awareness
paragraphs: The Community Oral Health Awareness Programme was organised to promote oral hygiene and highlight its importance in maintaining overall health and well-being. Dental professionals conducted awareness sessions on preventive dental care, proper brushing and flossing techniques, affordable dental treatment options, and advancements in dentistry. Practical demonstrations using dental models enabled students to understand and practise appropriate oral hygiene methods. Interactive discussions, question-and-answer sessions, individual consultations, and the distribution of oral hygiene kits further strengthened the programme’s educational impact.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being by promoting preventive healthcare, improving awareness of oral diseases, and encouraging healthy daily practices. It also helped students understand the relationship between oral health and general well-being. The programme strengthened school–community and healthcare partnerships by connecting students with dental professionals and accessible dental care resources.

contentBlocks.title: Community Outreach Programme on Stress Management for Nursing Students
paragraphs: The community organisation programme on Stress Management for GDA Nursing Students was conducted to create awareness about the causes, symptoms, and effects of stress and to equip students with practical coping strategies for academic and personal challenges. The session, led by Sr Leema, addressed stress management, time management, relaxation techniques, positive thinking, and self-confidence. Interactive discussions and relaxation exercises encouraged active participation and enabled students to identify sources of stress and explore effective coping mechanisms.

The programme directly contributes to SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being, particularly by promoting mental health awareness and emotional well-being among young learners. It encouraged students to recognise stress, communicate their concerns, and adopt healthy coping practices. The initiative also demonstrated the application of social work knowledge through counselling principles, communication, group facilitation, and community engagement.

contentBlocks.title: Awareness Session on Drug Abuse and Rehabilitation
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, School of Humanities and Social Sciences, Kristu Jayanti College, in collaboration with BREADS (Bangalore Rural Educational and Developmental Society), a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), under the MINDS Project, organised an Awareness Session on Drug Abuse and Rehabilitation on 4 November 2025, from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM, at Mariam Nivas High School, 10, Milton Street, D Costa Layout, Cooke Town, Bengaluru – 560005. The programme was conducted by first-year MSW student trainees (25MSWA17 and 25MSWA36) under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce. Ms. Pranitha P. S., Project Coordinator at BREADS, served as the resource person and addressed the causes and consequences of substance abuse among adolescents, preventive strategies, early intervention and the importance of rehabilitation and community support. Through interactive discussions and real-life examples, the session sensitised students to the harmful effects of drug abuse, peer influence and the importance of healthy coping mechanisms. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, particularly the prevention of substance abuse and the promotion of mental health and well-being. The collaboration with BREADS and its MINDS Project demonstrates the university's partnership with an NGO in strengthening community-based mental health awareness, preventive education and rehabilitation initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Emotional Well-Being Among the Elderly
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), organised an Awareness Session on Emotional Well-Being Among the Elderly on 13 November 2025 at Grace Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, with the participation of first-year MSW student trainees (25MSWA29 and 25MSWA31) under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce. Dr. Sandra K. S., Medical Officer and Manager at Grace Hospital, served as the resource person and conducted an interactive session addressing common emotional and psychological challenges experienced during old age, including loneliness, anxiety and depression. The session highlighted the importance of emotional stability, stress management, self-care, positive thinking and family and community support in promoting healthy ageing. Through interactive discussions and experience-sharing, elderly participants were encouraged to express their feelings, recognise emotional health concerns and adopt appropriate coping strategies. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, particularly the promotion of mental health, psychological well-being and healthy ageing. The programme also strengthened community awareness of the emotional needs of older adults and reinforced the university's commitment to inclusive, community-oriented health and well-being initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Building Emotional Resilience Among Mothers of Children with Special Needs
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Tamahar Trust, Bengaluru, a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), organised a Community Organisation Programme titled “Building Emotional Resilience” on 14 November 2025, from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM, at Tamahar Outreach, Madanayakanahalli, Bengaluru, benefiting 15 mothers of children with special needs. The programme was organised by II MSW students, with Ms. Gayatri Rao, Consultant Psychologist at Tamahar Trust, serving as the resource person. The session focused on strengthening the emotional resilience of caregivers by addressing stress management, self-care, positive communication, healthy coping mechanisms and the importance of family and community support networks. Interactive discussions and experience-sharing activities provided mothers with a supportive platform to express their caregiving challenges, develop mutual understanding and overcome feelings of isolation. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, particularly mental health promotion and psychological well-being among caregivers of children with special needs. The collaboration with Tamahar Trust highlights the university's engagement with an NGO in providing community-based emotional support, strengthening caregiver resilience and promoting inclusive health and well-being.

contentBlocks.title: Innovative Approaches to Mathematics Education
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Akshara Foundation, a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO) working towards improving the quality of education, and Jeeyar Memorial School, organised an educational outreach programme titled “Innovative Approaches to Mathematics Education” on 3 November 2025 at Jeeyar Memorial School, B. Channasandra, Bengaluru. The programme was facilitated by first-year MSW student trainees Christine Anna Kurien and New Life B, under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce. Mr. Shivakumar served as the resource person and introduced innovative, child-friendly and activity-based approaches to mathematics education through games, puzzles, visual aids and hands-on activities focusing on arithmetic operations, logical reasoning and problem-solving skills. The interactive activities encouraged students to participate enthusiastically, develop mathematical curiosity and gain confidence in understanding mathematical concepts. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting inclusive, equitable and effective learning opportunities through experiential and participatory teaching methods. The collaboration with Akshara Foundation highlights the university's partnership with an NGO in strengthening educational outreach and improving learning experiences among school students through innovative pedagogical practices.

contentBlocks.title: Awareness session on “ Building Reading Habits In Children ”
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Vathsalya Charitable Trust, a non-governmental organisation (NGO), organised a Community Organisation Programme titled “Building Reading Habits in Children” on 4 November 2025 at Vathsalya Charitable Trust, Bengaluru. The programme was facilitated by first-year MSW student trainees Kesang Chhoden and Sreelakshmi Ramesh under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce A. Ms. Santi, Manager of the Community Development Centre (CDC), served as the resource person and highlighted the importance of reading in developing children's knowledge, imagination, creativity, language skills and moral values. Through interactive discussions, storytelling and experience-sharing activities, children were encouraged to explore books, share their favourite stories and develop reading as a regular habit. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting foundational literacy, inclusive learning opportunities and a culture of lifelong learning among children. The collaboration with Vathsalya Charitable Trust highlights the university's engagement with an NGO in strengthening community-based educational initiatives and encouraging reading practices among children. The programme resulted in increased enthusiasm for reading, greater awareness of its educational benefits and motivation among children, teachers and caregivers to sustain regular reading activities.

contentBlocks.title: Life Skills Session – “My Dream, My Future”
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Global Concerns India, a non-governmental organisation (NGO), organised a Life Skills Development Programme titled “My Dream, My Future” on 10 November 2025 at the Global Concerns India – Children Creativity Centre. The programme was facilitated by first-year MSW student trainees (25MSWA01 and 25MSWA25) under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce, with support from Dr. Sadhana Dash Philip, Organisation Supervisor, and Programme Coordinators Ms. Maria Subrahmaniam and Ms. Zeena Mani. The session focused on developing essential life skills, including communication, decision-making, problem-solving, empathy, self-awareness and emotional management, in accordance with the core life skills framework of the World Health Organization (WHO). Through visual presentations, interactive discussions and activities encouraging students to introduce themselves and share their future ambitions, the programme promoted confidence, positive thinking, self-expression and goal-setting. The initiative directly contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting inclusive, holistic and learner-centred education through the development of essential life skills and competencies. The collaboration with Global Concerns India highlights the university's partnership with an NGO in extending meaningful educational and personal development opportunities to children through community-based learning initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Awareness session on `Mindful Screen Use – Using Technology Wisely for Learning Purposes.”
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, organised a Community Organisation Programme titled “Mindful Screen Use – Using Technology Wisely for Learning Purposes” on 11 November 2025 at Sukrupa School Educational Centre, Bengaluru, with the participation of first-year MSW student trainees Annriya J. Kunnath V. S. and Shelly Pyngrope Phawa, under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce A. The session was facilitated by Ms. Mohana Priya, who sensitised students and parents to the productive use of digital technology for learning while addressing the consequences of excessive screen exposure, including reduced concentration, sleep disturbances and increased stress. Through interactive discussions, demonstrations and reflective activities, participants learned practical strategies such as setting screen-time limits, taking regular breaks, selecting educational content and maintaining responsible digital habits. The initiative contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting digital literacy, responsible technology use and equitable access to technology-supported learning. The programme also strengthened awareness among parents and students about creating healthy digital learning environments at home, encouraging technology to serve as an effective educational resource rather than a distraction.

contentBlocks.title: Sustainova 2025: Promoting Sustainability Awareness and Education through Student-Led Innovation
paragraphs: The UNAI SDG Hub 10 – Vice-Chair for Teaching and Education of Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) organised Sustainova 2025, an intra-university sustainability fest on 24 September 2025, with the participation of 130 beneficiaries. The initiative provided a student-centred platform to promote awareness and understanding of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals through creative, experiential and collaborative learning. The major events included InnoViron Expo, SDG Policy Architects, Eco Vogue Runway and Quest for 17, encouraging students to explore sustainability challenges and develop innovative responses. As part of the InnoViron Expo, students exhibited creative models representing all 17 SDGs, translating their understanding of global sustainability concerns into practical and visual learning experiences. The programme encouraged critical thinking, innovation, teamwork and responsible citizenship while strengthening students' understanding of sustainable development. Through these educational activities, the university contributed to SDG 4 (Quality Education), particularly Target 4.7, by fostering knowledge, awareness and competencies essential for sustainable development.

contentBlocks.title: Insurance for Independence- A financial Safety for Women
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Shishumandir, Bengaluru, organised a community outreach programme titled “Insurance for Independence – Financial Security for Women” on 5 November 2025 at Shishumandir, Bengaluru. The programme was coordinated by first-year MSW students bearing roll numbers 25MSWA12, 25MSWA15 and 25MSWA43, under the guidance of faculty in-charge Dr. Winnie Joyce. Mr. Loganathan S. served as the resource person. The session was conducted for women e-auto drivers to create awareness about the importance of financial protection and independent financial planning. It covered various aspects of life, health and vehicle insurance, including policy benefits, enrolment procedures, premium payments, claim processes and available government and private insurance schemes. The programme aimed to strengthen women's financial literacy, promote informed financial decision-making and improve their access to financial protection mechanisms. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 5: Gender Equality, particularly by supporting women's economic empowerment, financial independence and equal opportunities to access financial services and security mechanisms.

contentBlocks.title: Community Organisation Programme on “Basic Hygiene and Sanitation for School Children”
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with Bosco Nivas, organised a community awareness programme on “Basic Hygiene and Sanitation for School Children” at St. Xavier’s High School, Shivajinagar, Bengaluru, on 31 October 2025. The programme educated school children on personal hygiene, proper handwashing techniques, oral hygiene, cleanliness, the use of sanitary toilet facilities, and the importance of safe drinking water. Through interactive discussions, visual demonstrations, and awareness activities, the programme promoted healthy hygiene practices and highlighted their role in preventing communicable diseases. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, particularly Target 6.2, by promoting adequate sanitation and hygiene practices and fostering awareness of their importance in maintaining healthy communities.

contentBlocks.title: Community Organisation Programme on “Fostering Sustainable and Resilient WASH Practices”
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru, in collaboration with SOS Children’s Villages India, organised a community awareness programme on “Fostering Sustainable and Resilient WASH Practices” at Lingarajapuram, Bengaluru, on 1 November 2025, benefiting 30 participants. The session, facilitated by Mr. Sathish K. N., Program Manager, Catalyst Management Service, focused on promoting sustainable Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) practices. Through interactive demonstrations, handwashing action songs, animated videos and group drawing activities, children were educated on the importance of safe drinking water, proper sanitation, personal hygiene, responsible water use and maintaining clean surroundings. The programme also highlighted the importance of healthy eating habits in promoting overall well-being. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, particularly Targets 6.1 and 6.2, by strengthening awareness of safe water, sanitation and hygiene practices and encouraging children to adopt responsible behaviours for healthier and more sustainable communities.

contentBlocks.title: Community Organisation Programme on “Financial Literacy and Career Guidance”
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with MYRADA (Mysore Resettlement and Development Agency), organised a community outreach programme on “Financial Literacy and Career Guidance” at St. Mary’s School and Composite PU College, Byrathi, Bengaluru, on 13 November 2025, benefiting 120 students from the Arts, Commerce, Science and Languages streams. Facilitated by Ms. Riya Shaji Mathew, Vocational Trainer and Executive Programme Coordinator at Akshadhaa Foundation, the programme focused on developing students’ financial management skills and enhancing awareness of diverse career opportunities. The session covered essential financial concepts, including budgeting, saving and financial planning, while guiding students to make informed career choices based on their interests, aptitude and emerging employment opportunities. The initiative directly contributes to SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, particularly Target 8.6, by equipping young people with career awareness, employability-related knowledge and essential financial skills, thereby encouraging informed career decisions and supporting their transition towards productive employment and economic independence.

contentBlocks.title: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan – One District One Product (ODOP) Scheme: Campus Farmers’ Market (CFM) – Farmers to Students (F2S)
paragraphs: Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous), under Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA), organised the Campus Farmers’ Market (CFM) under the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative on 31 January 2025, as part of the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The programme, themed “From Farmers to Students: Growing Knowledge, Nourishing Futures,” aimed to strengthen the connection between rural farmers and urban consumers while promoting local agricultural products, rural entrepreneurship and sustainable economic development. The event was inaugurated in the presence of Shri Pradeep Simha, District Officer, Minority Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, and provided a platform for 12 farmers from different districts to showcase and directly market their agricultural produce, organic goods and traditional food products. The Campus Farmers’ Market benefited over 5,000 individuals by facilitating access to local produce, promoting farmer-consumer interactions and creating awareness about supporting local agricultural economies. By providing market access to rural producers, encouraging entrepreneurship and reducing intermediary barriers, the initiative directly contributes to SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, particularly Target 8.3, which promotes productive activities, entrepreneurship, innovation and the growth of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. It also supports inclusive economic opportunities and sustainable rural livelihoods.

contentBlocks.title: NSS Community Outreach Programme – Visit to Neha Jyothi Ashram
paragraphs: The National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of Kristu Jayanti College organised a community outreach programme at Neha Jyothi Ashram on 8 March 2025, benefiting 15 children. The initiative aimed to promote compassion, social responsibility and inclusive community engagement through donation and interactive activities. NSS volunteers from two student teams collectively mobilised donations worth ₹2,000 and provided essential items and snacks to the children. The volunteers also engaged the children through storytelling, musical chairs, passing-the-ball games, singing and dancing activities, encouraging their creativity, self-expression and social interaction. Prizes were distributed to the winners, making the visit a joyful and meaningful experience. The initiative fostered a spirit of volunteerism, kindness and community participation while promoting the inclusion and well-being of vulnerable children. The programme contributes to SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, by encouraging the social inclusion and participation of vulnerable groups through community engagement and supportive interventions.

contentBlocks.title: Harmony in Diversity: Art and Music Activities For Differently Abled Children
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, in collaboration with Oceanik Institute of Higher Education, Bengaluru, organised a community engagement programme titled ‘Harmony in Diversity: Art and Music Activities for Differently Abled Children’ on 1 November 2025. Organised by student trainees Sheetal Pattanashetti and Mohammed Fasil, under the guidance of Mrs. Maheshwari, the programme aimed to promote inclusion, creativity, self-expression, and social interaction among differently abled students, including those with hearing and visual impairments. Facilitated by Dr. N. M. Poovaiah, the session incorporated singing and art activities that provided participants with opportunities to showcase their talents, express themselves creatively, and engage in collaborative experiences. The programme created a supportive and inclusive environment that encouraged confidence, mutual understanding, and meaningful participation among students.

The initiative directly contributes to SDG 10 – Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, which focuses on empowering and promoting the social inclusion of all individuals, irrespective of age, disability, or other status. By providing differently abled children with equal opportunities to participate in artistic and musical activities, the programme promoted accessibility, recognition of individual abilities, and social integration. It also challenged barriers to participation by creating an inclusive platform where students could express their talents and interact without discrimination. The initiative reflects the University's commitment to disability inclusion, equal opportunities, diversity, and the promotion of an inclusive and equitable society.

contentBlocks.title: Emergency and Safety Skill for Young Adults with Intellectual Disabilities
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, conducted a community awareness programme titled ‘Emergency and Safety Skills for Young Adults with Intellectual Disabilities’ on 4 November 2025 at Diya Foundation, Bengaluru, involving first-year MSW students. The programme engaged 28 beneficiaries and aimed to enhance their awareness and preparedness in responding to emergencies. The session covered physical, emotional, and personal safety, identification of emergency services, and appropriate responses to situations such as fire accidents, gas leaks, and medical emergencies. Through visual aids, practical explanations, and demonstrations, participants were introduced to emergency contact procedures using the 4 W's, fire safety measures, emergency evacuation practices, basic life-saving techniques, and the importance of seeking immediate assistance. The initiative focused on strengthening the beneficiaries' confidence, independence, and ability to respond safely to emergency situations.

The programme directly contributes to SDG 10 – Reduced Inequalities, particularly Target 10.2, which aims to empower and promote the social, economic, and political inclusion of all individuals, irrespective of age, disability, or other status. By providing young adults with intellectual disabilities access to essential safety education and practical emergency preparedness skills, the initiative promoted equal access to knowledge, personal security, and independent living. It also addressed the specific learning and safety needs of persons with intellectual disabilities, encouraging their active participation and integration into society. The programme reflects the University's commitment to disability inclusion, empowerment, equal opportunities, and the development of a safer and more supportive community.

contentBlocks.title: Launch of 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (VADP) under Unnat Bharat Abhiyan – Viksit Bharat @2047
paragraphs: The Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA), Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous), launched the 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (VADP) on 23 January 2025 as part of the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The initiative aims to promote holistic and sustainable development across 25 adopted villages through community participation, capacity building and integrated rural development. The programme focuses on improving community well-being through health and sanitation initiatives, skill development, women's empowerment, rural entrepreneurship, livelihood promotion and environmental sustainability. It also emphasises strengthening local leadership, encouraging renewable energy adoption, promoting sustainable agricultural practices and improving waste management. By fostering active community participation and addressing the social, economic and environmental needs of rural populations, the initiative seeks to create inclusive, resilient and sustainable communities. The programme contributes to SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities, particularly Target 11.a, by promoting integrated rural development and strengthening the linkages between urban and rural communities through sustainable development initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: Fire Safety Awareness Programme and Mock Drill – Karnataka Civil Defence Corps
paragraphs: The Karnataka Civil Defence Corps (KCDC) of Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous), under Jayantian Extension Services, organised a Fire Safety Awareness Programme and Mock Drill on 2 March 2025, benefiting 48 participants, including KCDC volunteers and villagers. The programme was conducted by the Kolar Fire Safety Team, which provided practical demonstrations on fire prevention, the classification and usage of fire extinguishers, and emergency response procedures. Participants gained hands-on exposure to firefighting equipment, fire engines and different types of water hoses through a live mock drill. The session enhanced awareness of fire hazards, emergency preparedness and the importance of timely and coordinated action during fire-related incidents. The initiative strengthened community resilience by equipping volunteers and villagers with essential knowledge and practical skills to respond to emergencies. The programme directly contributes to SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities, particularly Target 11.5, by promoting disaster preparedness and strengthening community-level capacity to reduce the impact of disasters and emergencies.

contentBlocks.title: Child Rights and Protection
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti University, conducted a community organisation programme on ‘Child Rights and Protection’ on 29 October 2025 at Sneha Jyothi Ashraya, Bengaluru, involving 11 students. The programme aimed to sensitise children, including orphans and children with special needs, about their fundamental rights, personal safety, safe and unsafe situations, and the importance of mutual respect. Through interactive discussions, storytelling, simple examples, and question-and-answer activities, the MSW students facilitated an engaging learning environment that encouraged children to express themselves and understand their rights. The session also focused on building children's confidence to communicate concerns and approach trusted individuals for assistance. The programme extended its awareness-building efforts to caregivers and the surrounding community, emphasising their collective responsibility in ensuring children's safety, dignity, and protection.The initiative directly contributes to SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, particularly Target 16.2, which aims to end abuse, exploitation, trafficking, and all forms of violence against children. By educating children about their rights, personal safety, and mechanisms for seeking help, the programme strengthened awareness of child protection and prevention of abuse. The observed improvement in children's confidence, ability to recognise unsafe situations, and willingness to express themselves highlights the programme's contribution towards fostering a safe, inclusive, and protective environment. The initiative reflects the University's commitment to promoting children's rights, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and strengthening community responsibility towards child protection.

contentBlocks.title: Community Organisation Programme on “Safe Touch and Unsafe Touch”
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), in collaboration with MANNA – Centre for Special Needs Children, Bengaluru, organised a community awareness programme on “Safe Touch and Unsafe Touch” on 4 November 2025 for especially abled children. Facilitated by Ms. Nirmala Jacob, Coordinator of Exodus Transitional School, the programme aimed to create awareness about body safety, personal boundaries and child protection through age-appropriate and interactive learning methods. Using skits, discussions and colouring activities, children were sensitised to identifying safe and unsafe physical contact, expressing discomfort, recognising potentially harmful situations and approaching trusted adults for support. The initiative strengthened awareness of child rights, personal safety and preventive measures against abuse and exploitation. The programme directly contributes to SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, particularly Target 16.2, which focuses on ending abuse, exploitation, trafficking and all forms of violence against children.

contentBlocks.title: Social Media Awareness and Its Impact on Urban Slum Students
paragraphs: The Department of Social Work, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru, in collaboration with Brothers Integrated Rural Development Society (BIRDS), a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), organised a Community Organisation Programme titled “Social Media Awareness and Its Impact for Urban Slum Students” on 23 September 2025 at Maria Tuition Centre, Jalahalli, Bengaluru, benefiting 30 students from the urban slum community. The programme was conducted under the faculty guidance of Dr. Winnie Joyce A, with Mr. Gnana Prakash, Rural Coordinator, serving as the resource person. The session focused on educating students about the positive educational uses of social media, including communication, learning and skill development, while addressing associated risks such as misinformation, excessive usage and irresponsible online behaviour. An interactive chart presentation encouraged students to share their experiences, develop critical thinking and understand the importance of responsible digital practices. The initiative contributed to SDG 4: Quality Education, particularly by promoting inclusive learning opportunities, digital awareness and the development of essential digital literacy and critical thinking skills among students from an underserved urban community. The collaboration with BIRDS highlights the university's engagement with an NGO in extending educational awareness and digital learning competencies to socially and economically disadvantaged communities.

contentBlocks.title: Yuva Pathshala: Promoting Inclusive Learning and Educational Support for Children in Underserved Communities
paragraphs: The Karnataka Civil Defence Corps (KCDC) Club of Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), through its Jayantian Extension Services, organised Yuva Pathshala on 16 and 23 October 2025 and 30 October 2025 and 8 January 2026 at Kacharakanahalli and K. Narayanapura slum communities, Bengaluru. The initiative engaged 55 student volunteers in providing educational guidance and interactive learning support to children from economically disadvantaged communities. Through educational games, drawing exercises and interactive teaching sessions, the programme aimed to stimulate creativity, strengthen learning interests, enhance confidence and encourage teamwork among the children. The initiative provided supplementary educational engagement in an underserved community, contributing to more inclusive learning opportunities and addressing educational disadvantages. It also enabled student volunteers to develop empathy, communication, teamwork and leadership skills through community engagement. The programme supports SDG 4 (Quality Education), particularly Target 4.5, by promoting educational inclusion and learning support for children in vulnerable circumstances.
